newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Orient-Avia doubles cargo in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Orient-Avia doubles cargo in 1996.

text.p: Russian private airline Orient-Avia carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996 after 95,800 passengers and 860 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1995, a company statement said on Monday.
Orient-Avia spokeswoman Yevgeniya Semerikova told Reuters the company planned to expand its international and domestic routes network during this year.
"We plan to make regular flights between Moscow and Chisinau, and non-stop flights from Vladivostok to St Petersburg and Kiev," she said.
Orient-Avia also planned to fly from Vladivostok to Honolulu and San Francisco in 1997, Semerikova said.
Currently, Orient-Avia runs a regular service between Moscow and Vladivostok and Petropalovsk-Kamchatsky in the Russian Far East. The company also operates the Moscow-Kaunas route.
The company's fleet consists of six aircraft, including four Ilyushin-62M long-range jets, one Ilyushin-86 wide-body plane and one Tupolev-134 jet. ZAO Orient-Avia was founded in 1994.
